summary: China's new rich list hits a record, and AI is the biggest driver: DeepSeek's founder debuts at seventh and Shenzhen now has more listed tycoons than any other city.
body: China's richest people are wealthier than ever, and AI is the biggest reason, according to the 2026 Hurun China Rich List, published on Tuesday by the Shanghai-based Hurun Research Institute [^1][^3]. It counts a record 1,529 people worth more than 5 billion yuan (about US$740 million), with combined wealth up 7% to US$4.8 trillion [^1]. Hurun says 160 people on the list, about one in ten, now make their money from AI, and the share from semiconductors also rose [^1]. ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming is first with a record US$99.7 billion [^1][^2].

The most watched newcomer is Liang Wenfeng, 41, founder of the AI lab DeepSeek, who enters at seventh with about US$42 billion; Hurun values DeepSeek at more than US$50 billion [^2][^3]. He was absent last year because DeepSeek presented itself as a research lab [^3]. Chen Tianshi of chipmaker Cambricon entered the top ten at US$30.5 billion, and Wang Xingxing of robot maker Unitree debuted at 78th [^1][^2]. For the first time, the tech hub of Shenzhen has more list members than any other city, ahead of Shanghai and Beijing [^1]. Some older tech fortunes shrank: Xiaomi's Lei Jun lost US$20.6 billion, and Baidu's Robin Li dropped out of the top 100 [^1].

My read: these fortunes reflect bets on China building its own AI and chips, and they sit beside a hard job market for young graduates, as yesterday's civil-service exam story showed. Wealth tied to share prices can also fall quickly if enthusiasm for AI cools.

reads.title: DeepSeek founder joins China's top 10 richest for first time with $42B fortune
reads.summary: Who DeepSeek's founder is, why he was missing from last year's list, and the AI and chip names rising on China's 2026 rich list.
